newsitem.title: USA: Mississippi Chemical Q4 at record levels.
newsitem.headline: Mississippi Chemical Q4 at record levels.

text.p: Mississippi Chemical Corp on Tuesday reported record results for the fourth quarter and year ended June 30, citing improved potash operations and delayed nitrogen sales.
Fourth quarter profits of $23.8 million, up 40.6 percent from a year earlier, came on sales of $173.5 million, were were up 39 percent from 1996's final quarter.
"We are pleased with our record fourth quarter results," said Charles O. Dunn, chief executive officer.
"The operational difficulties that were previously experienced at our potash facilities were largely corrected during the fourth quarter," he said.

"We also experienced heavy product movement for nitrogen early in the quarter as a result of carry-over demand from the third quarter, when sales were reduced substantially by unusually cool, wet weather. As the fourth quarter progressed, the company's results were negatively impacted by lower selling prices for our nitrogen products," Dunn said.

The carry-over demand was not as strong as anticipated due to a larger than expected switch in the company's primary trade area to soybeans from corn and cotton, the company explained. Soybeans do not generate a demand for nitrogen fertilizers.

During the quarter, the weighted average nitrogen sales price decreased by 5.0 percent from the prior-year quarter with all products showing a decline. The average selling prices for ammonia, ammonium nitrate, urea and nitrogen solutions were down 13.5, 10.2, 7.3 and 7.2 percent, respectively.
